generator: written by hand: Claude · Deck intelligence, October 18, 2026 (Linear ROB-114)
source: A first cut, to be corrected by measurement. The floors are the house minimums in crankmagic-rules.js ROLE_MINIMUMS (removal 8, wipe 2, ramp 10, draw 10; Rob, September 2026) and the land formula in crankmagic-change.js (38 lands, less one per two cheap ramp pieces, floor 33). The ranges around them follow the deck-building templates Commander players commonly use (about ten ramp, ten draw, five or more spot removal, two or more wipes, and a plan to win) and the published Commander Brackets (crankmagic-lobby.js BRACKETS): the lower brackets lean on fewer tutors and slower finishers; the higher ones on more ramp, protection and tutors. The reasonableness report (ROB-112) and the simulator's calibration (ROB-116) will move these numbers; until they do, each range is an opinion with a reason, not a measurement.

ramp.why: the house floor is 10; past 14 the deck runs out of things to spend it on

draw.why: the house floor is 10; a hundred-card singleton deck lives on its draw

removal.why: the house floor is 8 spot answers; three opponents bring more threats than one

counterspell.why: only when the deck plays blue; a few, because tapping out on your own turn is the Commander norm

wipe.why: the house floor is 2; the reset button for a board you are losing

protection.why: the engine and the commander kept alive: counters, hexproof granted, indestructible, blink to dodge

recursion.why: the pieces that come back after the wipe

tutor.why: consistency; too many and every game is the same game

threat.why: bodies that pressure life totals; below twelve the deck durdles, above twenty-five it has no answers

finisher.why: ways to actually end the game by card text: drains that scale, extra combats, you-win effects; most decks close with threats instead, so the floor is one

1.note: Exhibition: ultra-casual, no Game Changers, no tutors to speak of, slow finishes.

2.note: Core: precon level; the same restrictions; games run long and end on a big turn.

3.note: Upgraded: the base ranges; up to three Game Changers; a two-card combo only as a late finish.

4.note: Optimized: more tutors, protection and ramp; the strongest build of what the deck does.

5.note: cEDH: fast mana, dense interaction, every seat playing to win; wipes are rare, counters are not.

Balanced.note: The bracket's ranges as they are.

Aggressive.note: More bodies, fewer answers; wipes hurt the aggressor most.

Value engine.note: Card advantage and recursion over raw aggression.

Combo.note: Find the pieces, protect the turn.
